# **nfl4th** <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" width="25%" min-width="120px"/>

This is the package that powers the [fourth down calculator](https://rbsdm.com/stats/fourth_calculator/) introduced in [this piece on The Athletic](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2144214/2020/10/28/nfl-fourth-down-decisions-the-math-behind-the-leagues-new-aggressiveness/).

The code that powers the Twitter fourth down bot [is in this folder here](https://github.com/guga31bb/fourth_calculator/tree/main/bot) and the [code that runs the Shiny app is here](https://github.com/guga31bb/fourth_calculator/blob/main/app.R).

## Installation

The easiest way to get the released version of nfl4th is to install it from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=nfl4th) with:

``` r
install.packages("nfl4th")
```

To get a bug fix or to use a feature from the development version, you can install the development version of nfl4th from [GitHub](https://github.com/nflverse/nfl4th/) with:

```r
install.packages("nfl4th", repos = c("https://nflverse.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
```

or by using remotes:

``` r
if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("nflverse/nfl4th")
```


## Features

* The **go for it** model gives probabilities for possibilities of yards gained, including a touchdown, a first down via defensive penalty, and a failed attempt returned for a touchdown. It is built from smooth models of conversion, touchdowns, and where the play ends, fit on 3rd and 4th downs since 2001
* The **punt** model gives the probability of every spot where the receiving team can start, including touchbacks, blocked punts, penalties on the return, return touchdowns, and muffs the punting team recovers, fit on the last 8 seasons of punts
* The **field goal** model gives field goal % by distance, roof type and era, corrected for the fact that only teams that trust their kicker try very long field goals
* The **win probability** of the 1st down that follows each choice comes from nfl4th's own model, trained on 1st downs with the recipe of nflfastR's `vegas_wp`
* **Overtime** decisions follow the overtime rules of the game (sudden death, modified sudden death, or both teams getting the ball) using nflfastR's overtime win probability model
* **How sure is a recommendation?** `add_4th_probs(bootstrap = TRUE)` also values every play under 100 versions of the win probability and go for it models, each refit on a resampled history of games, and reports how often the call holds and an 80% interval for the gain from going for it

[How nfl4th makes 4th down recommendations](https://www.nfl4th.com/articles/articles/how-nfl4th-works.html) explains each of these in detail.

## Current limitations

* None of the models know anything about the two teams beyond the point spread and the over/under: not the kicker, the punter or the returner, the offense's short-yardage strength, injuries, or the weather
* Since 2020, the go for it model predicts late 4th & 8-10 attempts to convert about 3.5 percentage points more often than they did out of sample, so go recommendations there deserve extra caution
* A field goal that is blocked and returned for a touchdown isn't modeled: a miss gives the other team the ball at the spot of the kick
* The bootstrap measures sampling uncertainty, how much the models would change with a different history of games. Errors that every refit of the same models shares aren't in its intervals

## Get Started

To get started with nfl4th please see [this article](https://www.nfl4th.com/articles/articles/nfl4th.html), which also shows how to use the bootstrap output. Some examples of 4th down research using the package [can be found here](https://www.nfl4th.com/articles/articles/4th-down-research.html).
